threads.body: The cluster context is enabled in legacy mode too, so retries/redirections that previously produced one low-level span per attempted `Jedis` command are now folded into a single deferred span. That contradicts the linked requirement that legacy telemetry behavior remain unchanged. Please enable this aggregation only for stable database semconv and keep the existing legacy retry behavior (with corresponding legacy assertions).

replies.body:
Addressed in fad6f24ec9b7ff4c0732779df4154453518fa244.

Analysis: JedisClusterCommandContext.start() created a context in every semantic convention mode. That context suppressed the individual spans for legacy cluster retries and health checks. Limiting context creation to stable database semantic conventions restores the legacy command path while retaining stable-mode aggregation. The tests now assert the two legacy SET attempts on a reroute and the legacy PING health check before PUBLISH.

Upsides: Legacy telemetry keeps one span per low-level command. Stable telemetry still reports one aggregate command span with the final socket peer.

Downsides: The cluster tests now contain mode-specific span-count and endpoint assertions, which add a small maintenance cost.

threads.body: [General] Jedis 2.3 declares `JedisClusterCommand.execute()` with zero arguments, while this module supports `[2.0.0,3.0.0)`. For that version this advice never marks the command as executing, but `CommandAdvice` still creates a cluster context, so every low-level request is suppressed as a connection-acquisition command and the cluster operation emits no span. Match both the zero- and one-argument `execute` signatures (and ideally cover the 2.3 compatibility boundary).

replies.body:
Addressed in 72038d1b9564755de3974ccf9346db654ea66082.

Analysis: Jedis 2.3 declares execute() with no arguments, while later Jedis 2.x versions declare execute(String). The existing one-argument matcher left the stable cluster context outside its executing state on Jedis 2.3, so it discarded the command request. The matcher now accepts both signatures. A Jedis 2.3 test suite invokes a zero-argument execute method in both legacy and stable modes. The cluster-context unit test now runs only in stable mode because context creation is intentionally disabled in legacy mode.

Upsides: Jedis 2.3 cluster commands emit spans in stable mode. The dedicated compatibility test protects both execute signatures at the supported-version boundary.

Downsides: The new Jedis 2.3 suite starts an additional Redis container during check, which increases test runtime.

threads.body: [General] After the first cluster request is captured, this branch suppresses every later Jedis command on the thread, while `JedisClusterCommandContext.capture()` silently ignores commands whose operation/query differs. This leaks across blocking cluster subscriptions: Jedis 2.x invokes Pub/Sub callbacks synchronously before `runWithAnyNode()` returns, so an `UNSUBSCRIBE` or an unrelated Jedis call made by a callback loses its span in stable mode. Suppress only requests that belong to the selected cluster operation/retry (for example, by matching the captured operation/query); let nonmatching requests follow normal instrumentation.

replies.body:
Addressed in 3dd881c67d8fa3846f7eafe6bd80f1b33fb95922.

Analysis: Blocking Pub/Sub callbacks run while the cluster execute advice remains active. The connection advice must aggregate only requests whose operation and sanitized query match the captured cluster request. It must detach a different request from the cluster context so normal instrumentation ends that request's span.

Upsides: Cluster retries still update the aggregate peer address. Unsubscribe and unrelated callback commands keep their own spans in stable database semantic conventions.

Downsides: Matching compares two short request strings for commands sent while a cluster command is active.

threads.body: [General] When a slot has no cached pool, Jedis 2.x calls `renewSlotCache()` from `getConnectionFromSlot()` while both acquisition and execution are active. The resulting `CLUSTER SLOTS` send reaches this code before any request has been captured, so it becomes the deferred cluster-operation span and the actual command is emitted separately. Detach non-PING sends during connection acquisition before retry matching so refresh commands remain independent and the requested command is aggregated.

threads.body: [General] This also aggregates `execGetResponse()` in legacy mode. Jedis 2.9.3 implements that method independently (it sends `EXEC` directly rather than delegating to `exec()`), so before this change legacy telemetry emitted the low-level `EXEC` span; now this advice consumes the queued requests, suppresses `EXEC`, and emits a batch `SET`/`MULTI` span instead. That conflicts with the linked requirement that legacy telemetry remain unchanged. Please gate the new `execGetResponse` aggregation to stable database semconv and keep the legacy expectation in the test.
